title: Dynamics Reveals Structure: Challenging the Linear Propagation Assumption
claim: Logical negation of a query corresponds to a simple linear sign inversion of its gradient feature, so updates propagate coherently.
layout: 2 panels, left geometric sketch, right 2x2 commutative diagram with labeled arrows
description: The left panel is a geometric cartoon. A gray curved surface labeled Parameter Manifold carries a light-blue tangent plane at point θ. Two arrows start at θ. A blue arrow is the gradient φ_q = ∇s_θ(q). A red arrow points the opposite way and is labeled φ_¬q ≈ −φ_q. A dashed black arrow leads to θ+Δθ. A rounded box above states that after the update Δs(¬q) = −Δs(q). The right panel is a 2x2 commutative diagram of four rounded boxes. The top row is Query q ("T-Rex exists") and Negated Query ¬q ("T-Rex does not exist"), joined by a Log. Not arrow marked ¬. Vertical Linearize φ arrows lead down to Gradient φ_q and Inverted Gradient −φ_q. A Sign Flip arrow marked −I joins the bottom row. The eye goes first to the colored vectors on the left, then to the boxes on the right.
caption: Geometric interpretation of logical equivariance. (Left) A query q is associated with a score sθ(q) (e.g., log probability), and its gradient ϕq = ∇sθ(q) as a feature. Under the LPA, a local parameter update ∆θ induces a score change approximated by the inner product: ∆s(q) = sθ+∆θ(q) −sθ(q) ≈⟨ϕq, ∆θ⟩. Logical consistency under direction-agnostic first-order propagation requires that any local parameter change enhancing q suppresses ¬q (i.e., ∆s(¬q) = −∆s(q)), which necessitates that the gradient vectors be anti-aligned (ϕ¬q ≈−ϕq). (Right) This geometric requirement induces a commutative diagram where symbolic negation ¬ in the query space corresponds to a linear inversion −I in the gradient feature space.
abstract: Neural networks adapt through first-order parameter updates, yet it remains unclear whether such updates preserve logical coherence. We investigate the geometric limits of the Linear Propagation Assumption (LPA), the premise that local updates coherently propagate to logical consequences. To formalize this, we adopt relation algebra and study three core operations on relations: negation flips truth values, converse swaps argument order, and composition chains relations. For negation and converse, we prove that guaranteeing direction-agnostic first-order propagation necessitates a tensor factorization separating entity-pair context from relation content. However, for composition, we identify a fundamental obstruction. We show that composition reduces to conjunction, and prove that any conjunction well-defined on linear features must be bilinear. Since bilinearity is incompatible with negation, this forces the feature map to collapse. These results suggest that failures in knowledge editing, the reversal curse, and multi-hop reasoning may stem from common structural limitations inherent to the LPA.
